Safely delete plot features

safe_delete_plot_features.Rd

**DANGER: This permanently deletes data from the database!**

Deletes records of `data_liste_sub_plots`: the features of a plot, such as a census, a soil sample or a `principal_investigator` (see [query_plot_features()]). **The plot itself is preserved**, as are its individuals.

A plot feature can have things attached to it, and they are dealt with before the feature is removed: - its observation features (`data_subplot_feat`, e.g. the people of a census) are deleted with it - they describe nothing else; - measurements linked to it (`data_traits_measures.id_sub_plots` and `data_ind_measures_feat.id_sub_plots`, i.e. the measurements taken during a census) are **not** deleted. See `linked_measurements`.

**Safety features:** - Dry-run mode to preview what will be deleted - Refuses to strand census-linked measurements unless told what to do - Requires explicit confirmation (unless force = TRUE) - Uses a single database transaction (rollback on error)

Usage

safe_delete_plot_features(
  subplot_ids = NULL,
  plot_ids = NULL,
  types = NULL,
  linked_measurements = c("stop", "unlink"),
  con = NULL,
  dry_run = TRUE,
  force = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

subplot_ids

Integer vector. Specific plot feature record(s) to delete (`id_sub_plots` from `data_liste_sub_plots`). Takes precedence over `plot_ids`. Typically obtained from query_plot_features(plot_ids = ..., format = "long")$features_raw. Default NULL.

plot_ids

Integer vector. Delete the features of these plot(s) (`id_liste_plots`). Best combined with `types`. Default NULL.

types

Character vector. Restrict to these feature types (`type` from `subplotype_list`, e.g. `"soil_sample"`). Default NULL (all types).

linked_measurements

Character. What to do when individual measurements are linked to a feature being deleted (typically the diameters of a census): `"stop"` (default) refuses and lists them; `"unlink"` keeps the measurements and sets their `id_sub_plots` to NULL, so they no longer belong to any census. To delete them instead, use [safe_delete_individual_features()] first.

con

Database connection. If NULL, will connect automatically.

dry_run

Logical. If TRUE, shows what would be deleted without deleting. Default TRUE for safety.

force

Logical. If TRUE, skips confirmation prompts. Default FALSE. **USE WITH EXTREME CAUTION!**

verbose

Logical. Show detailed progress? Default TRUE.

Value

List with deletion summary (invisible). Includes `feat_info`, a data frame with one row per plot feature to be deleted (`id_sub_plots`, `id_table_liste_plots`, `plot_name`, `type`, `year`, `typevalue`, `typevalue_char`, `colnam`, and the counts `n_obs_features`, `n_measures`, `n_measure_features` of what is attached to it), `blocked` (TRUE when linked measurements stopped the deletion), and `error`, the database message, when the deletion failed.

See also

[safe_delete_subplot_obs_features()] to delete only the observation features of a plot feature, [safe_delete_plot()] to delete the whole plot.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- call.mydb()

# STEP 1: Extract the features and pick the ones to remove
feats <- query_plot_features(plot_ids = 123, format = "long",
                             con = con)$features_raw
ids_to_remove <- feats$id_sub_plots[feats$type == "soil_sample"]

# STEP 2: Always do a dry-run first!
safe_delete_plot_features(subplot_ids = ids_to_remove, con = con)

# STEP 3: Review output, then delete if sure
safe_delete_plot_features(subplot_ids = ids_to_remove,
                          con = con, dry_run = FALSE)

# Alternative: every soil_sample feature of a plot
safe_delete_plot_features(plot_ids = 123, types = "soil_sample", con = con)

# A census whose measurements must be kept, detached from it
safe_delete_plot_features(subplot_ids = 15063,
                          linked_measurements = "unlink", con = con)
} # }
